accessibility: The queue is a list of rows named by their status, author, title, place, anchor state, time and message count; the selected row carries an inset bar in addition to its tint.
Status is a glyph with its word, a missing Widget or Variant is an icon with words, and counts are text; nothing is carried by color alone.
The tabs are a labelled group with their counts; pressed quick filters and resolution chips expose their pressed state.
On a phone rows are 60px tall and inputs are 16px so iOS does not zoom.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Text, Button, Badge, Icon, Avatar, Segment, TextInput, EmptyState, Alert, Skeleton, Kbd, SegmentedControl); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.
Every Variant states what it shows through Widget visibility and selection only; the rows, groups, tab counts and chips of each Variant are the ones the app would show for that data.

The strings of the app are copied under the same Locale keys; names and ids bind through value and value2 and a sentence the app builds from translated pieces is one sample string per Locale. en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.

Buttons are 28px (the app's small buttons are 24px) and a pressed filter button shows a check with an outline where the app fills it; the Filters count is the button's own count pill; the saved filters and filter menus are in their own Views.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A member opened Reviews; the queue loaded every Review thread of the Workspace through the shared application facade and kept no canonical state in the browser.

The base state is the default Inbox tab: threads ready for review, then open threads, newest activity first, read by a member who may comment and resolve; Variants change the tab, the filters, the data and the member.

The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme. The queue is Workbench chrome, so its text follows the Workbench language and is baked here per Locale; names, View names, Widget ids and change domains are literal identities.
spec.intent: Show the Reviews inbox queue and everything that narrows it: status tabs with counts, resolution chips, search, quick and structured filters with their chips, saved filters, and the grouped rows, with the empty, caught-up, loading and error states and the member who cannot comment.
interactionRules: The header names the queue, says how many threads wait (ready for review and open, as the Overview does) and offers New comment to a member who may comment. Search filters by text and "/" focuses it; the Filters button carries the number of structured filters in use.

Mine and Updated are quick filters: Mine keeps the threads the member started or took part in, Updated those that changed since this browser last showed them. Saved filters opens the per-browser list of named filters; an active one is named on its button.

The structured filters (View, Variant scope, author, anchor, change domain) show as removable chips with Clear all. The tabs are Inbox (ready for review plus open), Ready, Open, Resolved and Dismissed, each with the count under every other filter; Resolved and Dismissed add chips for their resolutions.

Rows are grouped Ready for review, Open, Resolved and Dismissed and ordered by latest activity, newest first. A row shows its status glyph, the starter (initials, or a bot glyph for an Agent), the title, the starter and the View with its Variant scope (or the globe and Workspace), the anchor, a warning when the Widget or a Variant is missing, the change domains of a submission, the resolution, the time and the message count. Rows that changed since the member last looked are bold with a dot.

With nothing waiting the queue says so and offers Show resolved; with filters that match nothing it offers Clear filters, or the Inbox tab when only the tab is empty; with no threads at all it points to the Views. A failed load shows the error with Retry above the empty state, and loading shows placeholders.
The key legend (J K, R, E, O) shows only where a keyboard is expected: it and the "/" hint are hidden on a phone and when the single-key shortcuts are off.
